0.0.n: A polite conversational opener that gives the speaker a moment to frame their answer.

0.2.n: The speaker uses 自分 to refer to themselves rather than saying 私.

0.3.n: Marks the speaker as the topic; their main statement comes at the end of line 3.

0.4.n: Refers to people collectively, in contrast with AI.

0.5.n: Joins 人 and AI as the two groups coexisting.

0.6.n: Used alongside 人 as one of the participants in coexistence.

0.7.n: Marks 人とAI together as those doing the coexisting.

0.8.n: The adverb form of うまい describes how the coexistence happens.

0.9.n: The て-form of 共存する connects coexistence to the following description.

1.0.n: Identifies who can perform the jobs being described.

1.1.n: Pairs with a negative verb to exclude everyone or everything except 人.

1.2.n: Negative form of できる; with 人しか, the whole phrase means only humans can do it.

1.3.n: Described by the preceding phrase 人しかできない.

1.4.n: Casual form of という, used here to frame a category rather than give it a name.

1.5.n: Stands for the jobs just described, giving を something to attach to.

1.6.n: Marks the described jobs as what people do.

1.7.n: This second 人 identifies who actually carries out the work.

1.8.n: Marks 人 as the ones doing the jobs.

1.9.n: The て-form of やる links this action to leaving other tasks to AI.

2.0.n: Here AI is presented as a sufficient option for doing certain jobs.

2.1.n: In AIでいい, marks AI as the option that will suffice.

2.2.n: With で, expresses that AI will do, rather than saying the work itself is good.

2.3.n: The preceding AIでいい describes work that does not require a human.

2.4.n: Casual form of という, introducing the kind of work under discussion.

2.5.n: Stands for the jobs described by AIでいい.

2.6.n: Sets these jobs as the topic, contrasting them with human-only work.

2.7.n: This second AI identifies who receives responsibility for the tasks.

2.8.n: Marks the recipient of the responsibility in AIに任せる.

2.9.n: Plain form of the verb; the tasks being entrusted are understood from the topic.

2.10.n: Links the preceding arrangement to ような as a description.

2.11.n: In というような, presents the arrangement as an example of the world envisioned.

2.12.n: Lets よう describe a noun; the speaker resumes with そういった世界 in the next line.

3.0.n: Refers back to the arrangement of humans and AI described in the previous lines.

3.1.n: Means the envisioned society, not necessarily the physical planet.

3.2.n: Marks 世界 as what the speaker wants to create.

3.3.n: 作る changes to 作りたい to express the speaker's desire.

3.4.n: Adds a gentle, personal feeling to the wish, like thinking aloud.

3.5.n: Introduces the preceding wish as the content of the speaker's thoughts.

3.6.n: Part of というふうに, which frames the wish as the speaker's way of thinking.

3.7.n: Turns ふう into a phrase describing how the speaker thinks.

3.8.n: 思う + ています politely presents a view or wish the speaker currently holds.

4.0.n: Signals that the speaker sees the following point as expected or consistent with experience.

4.1.n: Refers here to international commerce, alongside importing and exporting.

4.2.n: Lists trade as an example rather than giving a complete list.

4.3.n: Combines 輸出, exporting, and 輸入, importing, into one word.

4.4.n: Links the trade and import/export examples to 領域.

4.5.n: Refers to a business sector or area of work.

4.6.n: Plain form of です, used before と to set up a context.

4.7.n: With だ, sets the field as the context for the examples that follow.

5.0.n: Adds emphasis to the speaker's description of routine work.

5.1.n: Means transferring existing information from one place to another, not specifically transcribing audio.

5.2.n: Combines with 転記 to name the activity of copying information.

5.3.n: Marks this task as one example in an unfinished list.

6.0.n: The name of Microsoft's spreadsheet software.

6.1.n: Marks Excel as the destination for the entered data.

6.2.n: Emphasizes that the work consists solely of the action that follows.

6.3.n: Plain form modifying 仕事; here it means entering data, not physically striking something.

6.4.n: Described by Excelにただただ打ち込む as work consisting of data entry.

6.5.n: Adds another example and leaves the list open.

0.lit: Well, yes, as for me, humans and AI coexist successfully, and…
0.tip: The て-form connects this idea to a longer sentence; the speaker's wish is not stated until line 3.

1.lit: Jobs that only humans can do, humans do, and…
1.tip: しか needs a negative verb, but 人しかできない means only humans can do it.

2.lit: As for jobs where AI suffices, entrust them to AI, that kind of…
2.tip: AIでいい means AI is sufficient, not that the job itself is good.

3.lit: That kind of world, I want to create, I think in that way.
3.tip: 作りたい expresses the wish, while というふうに思っています presents it gently as the speaker's current thinking.

4.lit: After all, when it is a field of trade and imports and exports…
4.tip: Noun + だと can set a context: when it comes to that field.

5.lit: Really, tasks of copying data and such…
5.tip: 転記 means copying existing information elsewhere, rather than necessarily turning speech into text.

6.lit: Work of doing nothing but typing into Excel and such…
6.tip: The entire phrase before 仕事 describes what kind of work it is.
